requirement:
The Python outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions and methods | `def` | Declared name |
| Classes | `class` | Declared name |

Nested definitions appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Decorators attach to the definition they decorate and are included in its
selected source and structural hash.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.python.items`.

**Item kinds and names**
- `python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements` in `outline/tests.rs` expects `def[f]`, `class[C]` and the method `class[C]/def[m]`.
- The same test asserts that the top-level `import` and `if` statements map to the root, so they are not items.
- `python_nested_definitions_use_the_nearest_outline_ancestor` in `tests/outline_content.rs` covers `async def`, which is exposed as `def[...]`.

**Nesting under the nearest enclosing item**
- The same test asserts the full selector list for these cases:
  - a class in a class
  - a method in a nested class
  - a function inside an `if` block inside a method, which attaches to `def[method]`
  - a class inside a function, with a method inside that class
  - an async function inside an async function

**Decorators in selected source**
- `python_selected_source_includes_its_decorators` asserts that the selected text starts with `@cache\ndef checked():`.
- It also asserts that the span start is 0.
- The nested test checks that the decorated method's selected text starts with `@decorate`.

**Decorators in the structural hash**
- `python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing` asserts that changing the decorator changes the hash.
- It asserts that removing the decorator changes the hash.
- It asserts that whitespace-only edits leave the hash unchanged.
- It asserts that a method decorator affects the class's structural hash.

**Selector rules**
- Selector syntax, percent-encoding and duplicate suffixes belong to the cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. That requirement has its own review, so I did not reassess it here.

**Decorated classes**
- No test decorates a class. In `outline/languages/python.rs`, `fn[attaches]` attaches any node of kind `decorator`, with no branch specific to functions or classes. A decorated class would behave the same way as a decorated function, so I did not count this as a gap.

I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} items
The Python outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Functions and methods | `def` | Declared name |
| Classes | `class` | Declared name |
Nested definitions appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Decorators attach to the definition they decorate and are included in its
selected source and structural hash.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
